source: Water-jacket worked example (test fixture, docs/data_formats/engine_thermal.md "Water jacket"): the generic 2.0 L I4 thermal file unchanged plus a water_jacket block, which splits the engine lump into metal and coolant joined by a pump-flow-dependent film coefficient. Every jacket number is [AS], sized for a 2 L passenger-car I4: wetted area 0.2 m2 per litre (0.4 m2: block cylinder liners about 0.13 m2 for four 86 mm x 86 mm bores, plus the head's coolant passages and the jacket walls); coolant volume 3.0 L per litre = the 3.0 L/L the class file's engine capacity already counts (so the metal lump is the class file's 25 kg/L x 630 J/(kg K) = 15750 J/K per litre exactly); htc_ref 5000 W/(m2 K) at a reference flow of 30 l/min per litre (60 l/min = the class pump at 3000 rpm), inside the 1000-20000 W/(m2 K) range forced convection of water/glycol in engine coolant passages reaches; flow exponent 0.8 (Dittus-Boelter, Nu ~ Re^0.8 at fixed geometry [C Incropera & DeWitt eq. 8.60]); floor 500 W/(m2 K) for natural convection with the pump stopped.
